context_methodology.scope: Current-week context only for the seven locked Stage 2 candidates.
context_methodology.note: Current-week context is qualitative evidence and does not represent a predicted probability.

context_factors.finding: Starting quarterback and near-every-snap player; Week 8 played 95% of offensive snaps and passed for 289 yards.
Minnesota has an aggressive pressure package, a 73% blitz rate and 25 sacks through seven games; it is allowing about 13.2 points per game.
Allen has completed 66% of passes against the blitz this season at 8.4 yards per attempt, with three passing TDs and three INTs.
LT Dion Dawkins (ribs) and LG Alec Anderson (ankle) are questionable; Spencer Brown has returned to practice and has no game designation.
U.S. Bank Stadium is indoors; outdoor weather is not a factor.

records.implication: The 200+ threshold has a strong locked historical record and Allen has shown he can attack blitzes, but Minnesota's pressure rate plus uncertainty on the left side of Buffalo's line create meaningful downside.

context_factors.finding: RotoWire lists Jones as Minnesota's lead back; in Weeks 5, 7 and 8 he averaged 12.7 carries and 2.0 targets per game.
Jones played 40% of snaps and had seven touches for 40 yards in Week 8, while Mason had eight carries and Dallas handled 34% of snaps as the passing-down back.
Minnesota continues to distribute snaps among Jones, Mason and Dallas. Demond Claiborne is ruled out, but his prior workload was limited.
Minnesota is starting Carson Wentz with Kyler Murray ruled out; that quarterback change adds uncertainty to the Vikings' offensive efficiency and likely play volume.
No game injury designation was listed for Jones in the official Week 9 injury reporting.

records.implication: The 25+ threshold is modest and Jones retains the nominal lead-back role, but the recent snap reduction and a genuine three-player rotation weaken confidence in predictable rushing volume.

context_factors.finding: Mason is listed as the change-of-pace back behind Aaron Jones.
Mason led the Vikings in carries in Week 8 with eight, but played only 14 snaps (28%); Jones had seven touches and Dallas played 34% of snaps.
Jones remains the lead back and Dallas has a distinct passing-down role. Claiborne is out, but had little recent usage.
No current Week 9 game designation was identified for Mason; no injury concern surfaced in the reviewed official report.
The Wentz-for-Murray quarterback change may affect play volume and rushing opportunity, but direction is uncertain.

records.implication: The 40+ CORE line needs a substantial workload relative to Mason's recent 28% snap share. The historical 7/10 is intact, but current role evidence is the weakest among the seven candidates.

context_factors.finding: Cook is Buffalo's lead back, with 138 carries through Week 8 and about 65% season snap share; he handled 21 carries for 80 yards in Week 8.
Cook played 54% of snaps in Week 8 and received 21 carries plus two targets; he remains the dominant share of Bills running-back touches.
Minnesota's aggressive blitz/pressure approach may encourage Buffalo to use the run game to keep the pass rush from teeing off; this is a tactical inference, not a guaranteed volume increase.
Dawkins and Anderson are both questionable, creating potential disruption on the left side of the line.
No Week 9 game injury designation was listed for Cook; he returned to action after a Week 8 evaluation and produced 21 carries.

records.implication: Cook has the strongest current workload evidence of the running backs in this game and cleared 70 yards last week. The two questionable left-side linemen are the main contextual risk.

context_factors.finding: Shakir leads Buffalo with 38 targets through seven games (19.7% team target share) and has 27 receptions; he averages 3.9 catches per game.
He caught five of six targets for 64 yards in Week 8 and played 67% of Buffalo's offensive snaps.
Shakir missed Friday's practice for a personal reason but returned as a full participant Saturday and has no game injury designation.
DJ Moore, Keon Coleman and Dalton Kincaid are also meaningful receiving options; Josh Palmer is ruled out, which removes one receiver from the rotation.
Minnesota's defense is first in points allowed and uses frequent pressure, a difficult overall defensive environment.

records.implication: Three catches is below Shakir's 3.9-catch season average, and his target role is stable. The elite opposing defense is a caution, but his recent usage and availability support the low Floor threshold.

context_factors.finding: Shakir has 38 targets through seven games (19.7% team share), 27 receptions and 354 receiving yards.
He recorded 64 yards on five catches in Week 8 and has averaged about 50.6 receiving yards per game this season.
He returned to full practice Saturday after a personal absence Friday and has no game injury designation.
Moore, Coleman and Kincaid are meaningful target competitors; Josh Palmer is out.
Minnesota is the league's top scoring defense and a high-pressure opponent.

records.implication: The 30+ CORE threshold is materially below Shakir's season receiving average, with consistent target involvement and recent production supporting it. Minnesota's defense is the principal negative.

context_factors.finding: Kincaid has 35 targets, 27 receptions and 401 receiving yards through seven games; he has played about 66% of Buffalo's offensive snaps this season.
He drew six targets in Week 8 but played 57% of snaps, with Dawson Knox playing about 70% and retaining a substantial role.
Kincaid was limited early in the week with a chest issue, then practiced fully Friday and Saturday and carries no game injury designation.
Minnesota's defense is first in points allowed and applies pressure at an unusually high rate.
The indoor venue removes weather as a receiving-condition variable.

records.implication: Kincaid's 25+ threshold is modest and his season production supports a usable role, but his Week 8 snap share was down and Knox remains heavily involved. The chest issue appears cleared for game designation purposes.

prior_stage_state.core_selection_rule: Choose FanDuel alternate with American odds -350 to -150 inclusive, closest numerically to -250; tie resolves to more negative price.
prior_stage_state.floor_rule: Immediately lower available alternate threshold than CORE.
prior_stage_state.ceiling_rule: Immediately higher available alternate threshold than CORE, regardless of HR.
prior_stage_state.historical_hr_rule: For every alternate Over line, hits = count of locked Stage 1 observations strictly greater than the listed alternate line; exact-line pushes are not hits; denominator remains N=10.
prior_stage_state.candidate_narrowing_rule: Carry forward if at least one Floor or Core alternate Over HR is >=7/10, aligned to the V7.2.9 minimum 70% historical HR required for final portfolio consideration. Exact-line pushes are not hits; denominator remains 10. No current-week context used for exclusion.
prior_stage_state.player_ordering_rule: QB → RB → WR → TE; within position sort P15 relative to the locked current main-market line: above first (smallest positive difference), equal next, below last (closest below first).
